newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz funds unit sees 50 pct growth in 97.
newsitem.headline: Allianz funds unit sees 50 pct growth in 97.

text.p: The fund management arm of Germany's largest life insurance company, Allianz Leben KAG said on Tuesday that it expects 50 percent growth in inflows into funds under management in 1997.

Klaus David, chairman of Allianz KAG, said the total under management was 23 billion marks ($13.5 billion) at the end of April, while in the first four months of 1997 the group had seen net inflows of 2.3 billion marks.

"We are confident that we will see those kind of rates over the whole year," David told a news conference, where the group announced a new range of different kinds of fund products, of which the equity fund was the cornerstone.
"Investors will be looking for more solutions in the future. The share will be the brick with which we will seek to build a range of products," said David.
The group's managing director Udo Frank said that shares offered a higher return than other investment vehicles.
Allianz KAG said that it had a 40 percent market share of the special funds business among life insurers, which made it the largest in that sector.
In the overall market its market share was 2.5 percent, which put it among the top ten.
Around forty percent of its investment in special funds was in equities, while around 43 percent was in German bonds. The amount invested in shares was on the increase, the group said.
In terms of bond-backed funds, central and eastern European, Latin American and southeast Asian funds were popular because of their high rates of return.
